info.title: Cheaper Inference API
info.description:
Wallet-backed, OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible inference. Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer ci_live_...` or `x-api-key: ci_live_...`. Both are accepted on every endpoint, and `Authorization` wins if both are present.

Every successful response carries a `cheaper_inference` object with the request id and what the request was billed. `billed_cost_usd` is a fixed 6-decimal string, not a number: a JSON float cannot round-trip a micro-dollar amount.

This document covers the customer-facing `/v1` surface only.

tags.name: Images
tags.description: OpenAI-compatible image generation and canary-gated image editing.

tags.name: Messages
tags.description: Anthropic Messages. Claude Code integrates here.

tags.name: Models
tags.description: The catalog, its capabilities and its prices.

tags.name: Usage
tags.description: What the workspace spent. Requires the usage:read scope.

tags.name: Account
tags.description: Wallet, savings, experiments, techniques, keys and connected chat channels. Reads need the account:read scope and changes need account:write; neither is on a key by default. This is the surface the MCP server drives.

tags.name: Docs
tags.description: The product documentation, searchable. Public content, so any valid key can read it without an additional scope. It exists as an endpoint so an assistant can answer 'how do I…' from the shipped text rather than from memory.

post.description: OpenAI-compatible. The request is optimized, served from the exact-match cache when possible, and billed against the wallet.

parameters.name: x-ci-techniques
parameters.description: Set to off to disable optional workspace techniques for a controlled benchmark. Preserves workspace defaults and billing policy; takes precedence over technique opt-in headers.

parameters.name: x-ci-prompt-cache
parameters.description: Prompt-cache knob. `passthrough` (default, or the API key's `prompt_cache_mode`) forwards the request unchanged; `on` additionally adds provider cache breakpoints for supported models. For Claude, unmarked requests cache the shared system/tools prefix and growing conversation; caller-supplied cache controls and lifetimes are preserved. `off` removes explicit cache controls and disables sticky affinity for this request; it does not disable a provider's implicit caching.

parameters.name: x-ci-prompt-cache-scope
parameters.description: Sticky-affinity scope: `session` (default), `user`, or `org`. Scopes the affinity key that keeps a repeated prompt prefix on the same upstream provider so its cache stays warm.

parameters.name: x-ci-prompt-cache-session
parameters.description: Session id read when the scope is `session`. Send one stable value per conversation or agent run. When absent, a string prompt_cache_key in the request body is used. Without either identifier, the tools, opening system instructions and first conversation message identify the session. Affinity remains isolated to the API key.

parameters.name: x-ci-vercel-provider
parameters.description: Opt-in strict Vercel upstream provider pin for operator-enabled model/provider pairs. Use the same provider ID on every request to retain provider consistency. Requires Core chat completions; fails rather than falling back to another source. Conflicts with API-key seller routing rules. Does not guarantee a cache hit or change the admitted customer price. Omit for normal routing.

x-ci-zdr.description: Whether zero data retention applied to this request. Absent when no policy was recorded.

x-ci-discount-percent.description: Quoted customer rate discount versus list, not the final effective savings after usage and optimizations. See usage history for the settled effective discount.

X-Cheaper-Inference-Request-Id.description: Request identifier. Legacy name, still emitted; identical to x-ci-request-id.

x-ci-tokens-saved.description: Input tokens removed by the optimizer.

x-ci-saved-usd.description: Total saved against the provider's list price, in USD.

x-ci-techniques.description: Comma-separated ids of the optimization techniques applied. Empty when none were.

x-ci-prompt-cache-affinity.description: Sticky prompt-cache outcome (KEA-5164). One of `hit`, `miss`, `new`, `stale`. Present only when the request carried a cacheable prefix and the affinity mode was not off; the exact-match `cache` header covers the separate response cache.

x-ci-experiment-variant.description: Name of the assigned experiment variant. Present only when the request included X-CI-Experiment and matched a running experiment.

x-ci-routing-overhead-ms.description: Elapsed milliseconds from proxy request start to dispatch of the successful provider attempt, including routing and prior attempts. On an exact-match cache hit, measures elapsed proxy processing time before returning the cached response. Present on successful buffered, streaming, and cached responses.

x-ci-model-response-ms.description: Elapsed milliseconds from dispatch of the successful provider attempt to its complete response body. Present on successful non-streaming responses; absent on streaming responses and when no provider was called.

x-ci-warning.description: Present when the request was served with a parameter value other than the one sent, because the model does not accept the value sent. Names the parameter, the value sent and the value used. Example: GPT-6 reasoning_effort "minimal" is served as "low". A request pinned to a provider is refused with 400 unsupported_parameter instead.

x-ci-stage-timing.description: Optional diagnostic timing breakdown, emitted when PROXY_STAGE_TIMING=1 and a request timer is active. Comma-separated stage=milliseconds entries with total first; zero-duration stages are omitted. Stage names depend on the request path.

post.description: Edit up to 10 source images with a 20 MiB decoded aggregate limit across the sources and optional mask. The OpenAI-compatible multipart form accepts `image` uploads and an optional PNG `mask`. The JSON extension accepts `input_references` containing HTTP(S) URLs or image data URLs; external URLs are passed only to compatible providers and are never fetched or stored by CheaperInference. Models are eligible only after a live edit canary; discover them through `capabilities.image_edit` on GET /v1/models.

post.description: OpenAI Responses, the surface Codex uses. Stateless: `store` must be `false`, and `previous_response_id` and `conversation` are refused. Replay prior output items in `input` instead. Namespace tools may mix function and custom/freeform entries, including inside `input[].additional_tools`; namespace and call metadata are preserved in buffered and streamed output. Gemini 3 requests using `reasoning_effort: none` fail with code `unsupported_reasoning_effort`. To use Pro, send a POST request to /v1/responses with store: false and reasoning.mode: "pro". Set reasoning.effort separately to control how much reasoning the model does. Pro requires the Responses endpoint. Chat Completions returns HTTP 400 for Pro requests. The models gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-5.6-terra, gpt-5.6-sol and gpt-6-astra support Pro mode. Set stream: true to receive output as it arrives, or stream: false to receive one complete response. These models use standard mode when reasoning.mode is omitted. For gpt-5.5-pro, the model ID already selects Pro. Omit reasoning.mode and set stream: false. This model does not support streaming. Your price, provider, region and data-retention settings still apply. The provider must also support the features in your request. If no compatible Pro provider is available, the API returns HTTP 503 without charging you. A provider response that does not confirm Pro is rejected without a charge. Other OpenAI Pro model IDs, model IDs with a date suffix, and Pro reasoning replay are not yet supported. This includes requesting reasoning.encrypted_content. Pro can take longer and use more tokens than standard mode. Billing includes the total input and output tokens used across its model work, so input_tokens can exceed your original prompt's token count. The gpt-5.5-pro model has its own pricing. For streaming requests, read the final event as well as the HTTP status. A stream can start with HTTP 200 and later report an error. Pro streams are charged only when a valid final response confirms Pro and includes token usage.

get.description: Every model this platform serves, with capabilities and prices. `pricing_version` is a SHA-256 over the list that was returned, so a filtered response validates its own cache and not the unfiltered one.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: `text` for chat models, `image` for models that generate something other than text.

parameters.name: vision
parameters.description: Select models that do or do not accept image input. Accepts 1/true/t/yes/y/on and 0/false/f/no/n/off.

parameters.name: video
parameters.description: Select models that do or do not accept video input. Accepts 1/true/t/yes/y/on and 0/false/f/no/n/off.

parameters.name: reasoning
parameters.description: Select models that do or do not reason. Accepts 1/true/t/yes/y/on and 0/false/f/no/n/off.

parameters.name: streaming
parameters.description: Select models that do or do not stream. Accepts 1/true/t/yes/y/on and 0/false/f/no/n/off.

parameters.name: zdr
parameters.description: `true` switches to the zero-data-retention view: only models a `zdr: true` request can be served for, priced at what that request pays. `false` (the default) is the standard view, not a filter for models without ZDR supply.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: Exact provider name, compared trimmed and case-insensitively. A prefix does not match.

get.description: The advertised catalog, with live prices, and NO API KEY. This is what the marketing pages and any other surface that cannot hold a key read. Prices are resolved by the same rule that bills a request, so a quote here and the charge cannot disagree. `/v1/models` covers the same catalog for authenticated clients and adds marketplace-only models.

503.description: The catalog could not be read. No prices are served rather than stale ones.

get.description: One catalog entry. The id may contain slashes (`google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite`) and is matched exactly, including case.

parameters.name: model_id
parameters.description: Model id. May contain `/`.

404.description: No such model, or it is not currently advertised.

503.description: The catalog could not be read. No prices are served rather than stale ones.

get.description: Per-request history for the calling workspace, newest first. Requires the `usage:read` scope. `cursor` is opaque and comes from the previous page's `next_cursor`; do not parse it.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page.

parameters.name: start_at
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound. A value with no offset is read as UTC.

parameters.name: end_at
parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound.

parameters.name: api_key_id
parameters.description: Limit to one key in the calling workspace. A key outside it is a 404, not an empty list.

post.summary: Record a refused request against the calling account
post.description: Reported by the MCP server when it refuses a call. `injection`, `escalation` and `policy` describe hostile arguments and trigger a permanent ban on the first occurrence, across every surface, not only the account API. `unauthorized` and `forbidden` describe a credential rather than an intent (a rotated key, a missing scope), so they are accepted and have no consequence. There is no rolling window, no warning tier and no escalation ladder. No scope is required. Returns the account's standing, and files a support ticket on the account's behalf so a block has somewhere to be contested.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code. Gemini 3 thinking cannot be disabled, so `reasoning_effort: none` returns `unsupported_reasoning_effort`.

max_completion_tokens.description: Alternative output-token limit. If both limits are supplied, they must match.

min_discount_percent.description: Price ceiling for this request as a minimum discount off the model's list price (see GET /v1/models pricing.list_*). Only supply priced under list × (1 − d) serves the request, and the bill is capped at that rate. With no qualifying supply the request fails with 503 `min_discount_unavailable` instead of falling back. Stripped before forwarding.

zdr.description: Route this request only through providers that support a zero-data-retention policy. A zero-data-retention provider does not keep your prompts or responses and does not train on them. The marketplace and every unverified provider are excluded, so the price is the ZDR price shown by `GET /v1/models?zdr=true`. Adds to the account's Data Protection setting; it cannot lift it. With no qualifying supply the request fails before it is sent upstream with 503 `zdr_capacity_unavailable`. Stripped before forwarding.

ranking.description: How the gateway orders the discounted sources that can serve this request. `discount`: cheapest first. `speed`: highest recent speed first, measured on this model from the gateway's own traffic (time to first visible output and output tokens per second, weighted towards the last hour); cost breaks ties. `balance` (default): speed score × discount. Speed and discount are NOT a trade-off: the fastest source is often also a cheap one, so `speed` can return the same route as `discount`. Fallback routes are not ranked. They are tried only when no discounted source can serve the request in time. The mode changes the order only, never which sources are eligible. Stripped before forwarding.

temperature.description: Model-specific sampling control. Omit on models that do not support sampling. Claude Chat-to-native translation caps values above 1 at 1.

top_p.description: Model-specific sampling control. Omit on models that do not support it.

n.description: Number of completions. Claude supports only 1.

reasoning_effort.description: Alias for reasoning.effort, including Claude. Conflicting values return 400. Supported levels depend on the model; Gemini 3 accepts minimal, low, medium, and high only. Claude native bridges translate effort into adaptive thinking or a manual budget within max_tokens. A manual budget must be an integer of at least 1024, strictly below the output limit. Thinking summaries, when returned, appear in message.reasoning_content or delta.reasoning_content. Native thinking and output_config settings take precedence.

reasoning.description: Portable reasoning controls, including Claude. false disables thinking where supported. Use /v1/responses for Pro. Chat Completions returns HTTP 400 for reasoning.mode: pro or an OpenAI Pro model ID such as gpt-5.5-pro.

exclude.description: For Claude Chat, true hides returned thinking summaries without disabling thinking.

max_tokens.description: Manual reasoning budget where supported. Claude requires at least 1024 and strictly less than the request output limit. Adaptive-only Claude models reject this portable budget.

thinking.description: Native Claude thinking configuration. Takes precedence over portable effort. Active thinking supports auto or none tool_choice, not required or a forced named tool.

output_config.description: Native Claude output configuration, including effort for adaptive thinking. Preserved by the native Chat bridges.

include_reasoning.description: For Claude Chat, false hides returned thinking summaries without disabling thinking.

cache_control.description: Request-level Claude cache control. Supported controls on tools, messages and content blocks are also preserved by native bridges. An opt-in does not guarantee a cache hit; off or ZDR removes explicit controls.

image_edit.description: True only after this model passes a live image-edit canary.

cache_read_input_per_million.description: Price per million prompt tokens read from the provider cache.

above_threshold.description: Conditional rates for the whole request when total prompt tokens, including cached tokens, exceed the threshold. applies_when states whether the serving supplier must also charge a long-context premium. Customer price caps still apply.

list_input_per_million.description: What the provider charges direct. Not on the legacy service.

zero_data_retention.description: True in the `?zdr=true` view: the rates are what a request carrying `zdr: true` pays, and only models a zero-data-retention supplier can serve are listed.

zero_data_retention_route.description: The model's zero-data-retention tier, in every view: `discounted` (ZDR served from discounted supply), `rail_only` (ZDR served only through a gateway route) or `none` (a `zdr: true` request is refused with 503 `zdr_capacity_unavailable`). Null only when the tier could not be read.

aliases.description: Vendor-qualified ids that also resolve to this model.

endpoint.description: Preferred inference endpoint for this model.

media_unit_price.description: Price per picture, for models billed per unit. Their token rates are not the price.

discount_percent.description: Measured from the price actually charged against the list price, on whichever basis bills the model. `0.00` means no list price is published to compare with.

supports_image_edit.description: True only after this model passes a live image-edit canary.

above_threshold.description: Conditional rates for the whole request when total prompt tokens, including cached tokens, exceed the threshold. applies_when states whether the serving supplier must also charge a long-context premium. Customer price caps still apply.

zero_data_retention_route.description: The model's zero-data-retention tier, in every view: `discounted`, `rail_only` or `none`. Same as `pricing.zero_data_retention_route` on `GET /v1/models`.

DetailError.description: The error body the /public routes answer with.

next_cursor.description: Opaque. Pass back as `cursor`; do not parse.

paid_amount_usd.description: Customer amount paid; null unless the request settled.

savings_usd.description: Customer-visible savings, always non-negative when present.

route.description: Always null. Identified the supply route that served the request; withdrawn because it names our supplier. The key remains so existing clients keep a stable shape.

serving_provider.description: Always null. Identified the serving provider; withdrawn for the same reason as `route`.

retention.description: Recorded request-time retention policy; unknown for historical requests without evidence.

effective_discount_percent.description: Effective discount against request-time list cost, including optimizations; null without comparable settled costs.

pricing_snapshot.description: Immutable customer and maker-list rates resolved at admission.

body.description: The section's full text. Present only on a search (`q`).

PricingChangeRates.description: Customer-facing rates on one side of a change. Null means the rate was not quoted at that point, which is different from zero.

prompt_tokens.description: Settled prompt tokens. Already includes any tokens served from the prompt cache.

cached_tokens.description: The share of prompt_tokens the upstream served from its prompt cache.

cache_reported_request_count.description: Settled requests whose upstream reported cache usage at all. Compare with settled_requests to see how much of the window cache_hit_pct speaks for.

cache_hit_pct.description: Percent of prompt tokens served from cache, over the cache-reporting requests only. Null when no upstream reported cache usage indicates an unknown rate, which is not the same as a reported 0%.

funded_by_owner.description: True when this member's usage is paid from the workspace owner's wallet.

tool.description: The MCP tool that was called.

kind.description: What was refused. `injection`, `escalation` and `policy` are refusals the MCP server issued itself and each count as a strike; `unauthorized` (401) and `forbidden` (403) are API denials and count once per distinct `detail`.

detail.description: A short stable code for the reason. Never the offending text.

strikes.description: Distinct strikes in the current window. This is what the tiers compare against.

attempts.description: Every denied call in the window, duplicates included.

remaining.description: Strikes left before the block. 0 while blocked.

blocked_until.description: When a timed block lifts. Null when not blocked, and null when the block is permanent. See `permanent`.

permanent.description: True for a block with no expiry: the daily limit was reached again within the repeat window of an earlier block. Only an admin lifts it.

prior_blocks.description: Earlier blocks on record that ran their course. One or more means the next block is permanent. A block an admin lifted does not count.

reported.description: True when this call filed the automatic support report for the account.

available_usd.description: Balance minus what is held against requests in flight. This, not balance_usd, is what can be spent right now.

AccountUsage.description: Rolled up over a window. Distinct from /v1/usage/daily, which is the per-day series.

saved_usd.description: List price minus what was billed.

windows.description: One entry each for the last 24 hours, 7 days and 30 days.

dimension.description: What the experiment varies: prompt, model or technique.

system_prompt_preview.description: Truncated to 300 characters. The dashboard has the full text.

available.description: Whether PATCH will accept it. False for preview and deprecated entries.

enabled.description: What the proxy will actually do for this account. Every implemented technique is off by default, so this is false until the account opts in.

explicitly_enabled.description: The stored choice, or null when the account has never set one.

changed.description: False when it was already in the requested state.

prefix.description: The first 18 characters. The rest is never recoverable.

key.description: The plaintext key. Also available to its owner through the dashboard's copy action.

available_events.description: The valid ids for the `events` field on PATCH, with their labels.

ChannelUpdateRequest.description: Both fields are optional; an absent one is left alone. `events: []` unsubscribes from everything, which is different from omitting the field.

sent.description: False with a `message` when there was no activity in the window. The request succeeded, but there was nothing to send.

candidates.description: Opaque per-response aliases: `primary` for the marketplace, `network_a`, `network_b`, ... for the others. Suppliers are never named.

data.description: Cheapest first. Ids that could not be resolved sort last with found:false.

list_usd.description: Null when no going-direct price is known for the model.

TopupResponse.description: Creates a Stripe Checkout session and returns its link. Nothing is charged here. The customer completes the payment on Stripe's own page.
